### Trace-level classification

Twelve classifiers, eight feature-based and four deep-learning, scored on a common test set of labelled PNW waveforms in four classes [@kharita2026]. Hatched bars are deep-learning models.

:::{figure} ../img/hazevalhub/quakexnet-classifier-comparison.png
:alt: Precision, recall and accuracy for twelve classifiers across earthquake, explosion, surface and noise classes
:width: 100%

Precision and recall per class, and overall accuracy. Figure from `notebooks/performance_comparisons_of_all_models.ipynb` in `Akashkharita/PNW_Seismic_Event_Classification` (MIT), Akash Kharita.
:::

Accuracy is close between the best deep models; size is not. Trained model sizes as recorded in the same notebook:

| Model | Size (MB) |
|---|---:|
| Scat(M2) | 436 |
| Scat+Man(M2) | 415 |
| Tsf(M2) | 291 |

| Phy(M2) | 289 |
| Phy+Man(M2) | 274 |
| Phy+Tsf(M2) | 289 |
| Phy+Tsf+Man(M2) | 291 |
| SeismicCNN(1D) | 40.9 |
| SeismicCNN(2D) | 7.96 |
| QuakeXNet(1D) | 2.65 |
| QuakeXNet(2D) | 0.306 |

The per-class scores behind the figure live in `results/*.pkl` files that are not in the repository, so the figure is the only public record of them (R7).

### The fifteen-year catalog

| Class | Located events, 2010–2025 | Median stations per event | Median distance from summit (km) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Surface events | 114,775 | 6 | 3.1 |
| Explosions | 13,766 | 5 | 3.7 |
| **Total** | **128,541** | | |

The fewest stations on any located event is 3; 8,133 surface events (7.1%) sit at that minimum.

:::{figure} ../img/hazevalhub/quakexnet-events-per-year.svg
:alt: Bar charts of located surface events and explosions per year, 2010 to 2025
:width: 100%

Located events per year. Station coverage changed over the period, so a trend here mixes activity with network growth.
:::

:::{figure} ../img/hazevalhub/quakexnet-month-of-year.svg
:alt: Line chart of the share of each class by calendar month
:width: 100%

Share of each class by calendar month. Surface events peak in October and are fewest in June; the peak month has 1.4 times the events of the quietest, a weak seasonal cycle.
:::

:::{figure} ../img/hazevalhub/quakexnet-hour-of-day.svg
:alt: Line chart of the share of each class by hour of day in UTC
:width: 100%

Share of each class by hour of day, UTC.
:::

Blasting happens in daylight, so the explosion class should crowd into Pacific working hours, 08:00 to 17:00 PDT or 15:00 to 00:00 UTC. A flat curve would put 37.5% of events in those nine hours. Explosions put 36.3% there and surface events 31.4%. There is no daytime excess, so the explosion class is not dominated by blasting. The time-zone bands here ignore the switch to PST in winter, which shifts them by one hour and does not change the conclusion.

### Against the PNSN catalog

PNSN analysts label surface events (`su`) and explosions (`px`). The comparison takes the 3,970 PNSN events of those two types, 2010 to April 2026, for which at least half the reporting stations lie within 50 km of the summit. A PNSN event counts as matched if the unfiltered QuakeXNet catalog of network detections has an event starting within 60 s of the PNSN origin time.

| PNSN label | PNSN events | Matched | Recall | Labelled `su` | Labelled `px` | Labelled `eq` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Surface event | 3,269 | 2,015 | 61.6% | 1,643 | 306 | 66 |
| Explosion | 701 | 596 | 85.0% | 144 | 434 | 18 |
| **Both** | **3,970** | **2,611** | **65.8%** | | | |

Of matched PNSN surface events, 81.5% carry the surface-event label; of matched explosions, 72.8% carry the explosion label. The two errors are not symmetric: 306 PNSN surface events were called explosions, against 144 explosions called surface events. The median offset between PNSN origin time and QuakeXNet detection start is 46.8 s, set by how detections are windowed and rounded to 10 s rather than by timing accuracy.

A second cut, from `notebooks/quakexnet_diagnostic.ipynb`, uses PNSN events whose location is within 70 km and lets a PNSN event match several QuakeXNet classes at once:

| Outcome | PNSN surface events | PNSN explosions |
|---|---:|---:|
| Correct class only | 2,495 | 390 |
| Correct class and another | 376 | 307 |
| Another class only | 167 | 73 |
| No detection | 244 | 63 |
| **Total** | **3,282** | **833** |

**Precision is not measured.** QuakeXNet finds 654,364 network events with no PNSN counterpart. PNSN does not try to catalogue every surface event, so these are a mix of real events PNSN never listed and false detections, and nothing on this page separates the two. That needs an independently labelled sample of novel detections.
